core_operating_system_directories.description: The central nervous system of your PC. It houses the critical system files, background components, and execution binaries required for Windows to function.
Located inside the main directory, this contains the core .dll (Dynamic Link Library) files and .exe applications essential for the Windows kernel and subsystem utilities.
On 64-bit systems, this folder handles the execution of legacy 32-bit software, allowing older applications to run smoothly alongside 64-bit architecture.
Known as the Component Store, it contains library files used to manage Windows updates, resolve software conflicts, and reverse system alterations.

application_and_shared_data_directories.description: The default storage directory where standard 64-bit applications install their files, executables, and supporting assets.
Found on 64-bit versions of Windows, this acts as the dedicated installation path for 32-bit third-party applications.
A hidden system folder that applications use to save settings, licensing profiles, updates, and configuration data shared across all users on the PC.

user_profile_directories.description: Holds all user profile directories created on the computer.
A hidden subdirectory under each user profile that isolates specific user application settings across three sub-folders: Local, LocalLow, and Roaming.

hidden_system_and_maintenance_directorie.description: A highly protected system folder used for storing system restore points, volume shadow copies, and search indexing databases.
Holds the local Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE) resources used to repair or reset the machine during boot failure.
A hidden system folder present on every drive partition that handles deleted files before they are permanently purged.
